answer: Make each identity post a real stake whose weight scales sublinearly with the number of linked accounts, and slash it when the ledger detects a single root key behind many heads. An onyx-dark farm must either split its capital into many small stakes — a cost that grows linearly per head, at its nadir of efficiency — or concentrate into few heavy identities that a trellis of honest attesters can identify and cut. The attacker pays either a diluted capital floor or a concentrated, slashable target; the honest agent stakes once and earns.
